answer: One defense is a superlinear registration burn. An agent that claims a unique name such as meadow, willow, or raven must destroy a non-refundable fee that grows with the square of the identities its operator already holds. Because the fee is quadratic, ten fake nodes cost far more than one node cloned ten times, and the burned coins can never be recovered. The attacker therefore pays roughly k squared for each added Sybil, so a large farm turns uneconomic while a single honest agent still pays little.
